solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get out or staying in?

definitions.meaning: to step down from a vehicle or horse is to get off or disembark
a fire that is still going is said to be staying in, i.e. burning

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is disembarking from a bus or train; the other is burning, as a fire that has not gone out.

clue.text: Superior yet out-and-out own goal is intercepted

indicators.note: the out-and-out word is broken into by the own goal, as a pass is intercepted

parts.note: arrant means utter, out-and-out
OG is the football abbreviation for own goal

explanation.surface: A football match report: a superior team, but an own goal is intercepted.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior attitude is a haughty, arrogant one.

clue.text: Romeo out of folly displays bad manners

indicators.note: Romeo's letter is taken out of the folly word

parts.note: imprudence is foolishness, folly
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo's foolish behaviour shows a lack of manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is cheeky rudeness, a show of disrespect.

clue.text: Promotion of extremely healthy exercise

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word are taken

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An advert promoting the very healthy benefits of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is extravagant publicity, a promotional campaign.

clue.text: Composer of famous suite "Queen's Arms" located here

parts.note: Gustav Holst wrote The Planets suite
ER is the Queen (Elizabeth Regina), with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A title in quotes, apparently a piece called Queen's Arms by the Planets composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title is a decoy: 'Queen's' gives ERS and 'Arms located here' defines the answer, since arms here means guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Holsters are the leather cases where pistols, i.e. arms, are kept on the body.

clue.text: Former lover still 1 across, it seems

definitions.meaning: something still alight is a flame that has lasted, so an old one

explanation.definitionFit: An ex-sweetheart is called an old flame; read literally it is a long-burning fire.

clue.text: Doesn't care about being poor

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned round and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who doesn't mind being poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-rate means inferior, of poor quality.

clue.text: Bush could be a church leader

definitions.meaning: a shrub with white flowers and dark berries
an official in some Presbyterian churches

explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a common shrub; an elder is also a lay officer of a church.

clue.text: Indian holy man, being dead, had us all bewildered!

indicators.note: the letters are thrown into confusion together

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on gravestones and family trees

explanation.surface: A holy man died, leaving the faithful bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu ascetic, a wandering holy man of India.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: a court hearing of a case

explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a court case heard before a judge, and also a test of performance.

clue.text: Decorate walls again about the same

indicators.note: the word turned about reads exactly the same, so it is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A decorator plans to redo the walls in much the same style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About the same' looks like a vague estimate, but it says the answer read backwards is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To paper a room afresh is to put new wallpaper on its walls once more.

clue.text: Marked document blocked by detectives

indicators.note: the detectives sit in the middle of the document, blocking it

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police detectives intercept a document that has been marked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Decided as an adjective means clear-cut or distinct, as in a marked improvement.

clue.text: Gallery displays heads of government outside Downing Street

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: DS abbreviates Downing Street, the London home of the Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A gallery shows portraits of government leaders outside Number Ten.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatres the gods is the highest gallery, the cheapest seats up near the ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: The topmost balcony of a theatre is called the gods, being closest to the heavens.

clue.text: Collapsed taking a bow — results in foot fault!

parts.note: something that has collapsed has fallen
a bow is a curved arch, as in a rainbow or an archer's bow

explanation.surface: A tennis player bows after collapsing and is called for a foot fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot fault' is a tennis term, but here it means a defect of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A flattened arch of the foot is a common medical defect of the foot.

clue.text: Change involves entire retraining for such surgeons

indicators.note: the change word wraps around the rearranged letters

parts.note: to vary is to change

indicators.note: retraining suggests reshaping the letters

explanation.surface: A change of career involves complete retraining for these surgeons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involves' means one piece surrounds another, and 'retraining' is the anagram signal; the surface's surgeons in training mislead.
explanation.definitionFit: Veterinary surgeons are animal doctors, so such surgeons are the veterinary kind.

clue.text: Arctic explorer Anne confused with the Poles

indicators.note: the letters are mixed up as if confused

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Anne mixes up a polar explorer with Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges ANNE together with N and S. 'The Poles' looks like Polish people but means north and south.
explanation.definitionFit: Fridtjof Nansen was a Norwegian who crossed Greenland and sailed the Fram towards the North Pole.

clue.text: Arab state up in arms after Middle East revolution

indicators.note: the angry word comes after the turned-round piece
a revolution turns the abbreviation round

parts.note: someone up in arms is angry, irate

explanation.surface: An Arab state is in uproar after a revolution in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up in arms' looks like part of a war story, but it simply means angry; 'revolution' turns the abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, such as those of the Gulf.

clue.text: Secondary flower

definitions.meaning: something that flows, i.e. a river

explanation.definitionFit: A tributary is a minor stream feeding a river, and as an adjective means subsidiary.

clue.text: Watch what's posted on line when drunk

parts.note: a letter posted is sent

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling around

explanation.surface: A drunk watching what gets posted online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb but is the noun for a guard; 'when drunk' is the anagram signal for the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard keeping watch, a lookout.

clue.text: Aim to please with tight fit

parts.note: tight with money is mean
fit and healthy is well

explanation.surface: A tailor eager to please with a snug fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean well is to have good intentions, even if things go wrong.

clue.text: Throw a twenty, say, to settle the score

definitions.meaning: to throw twenty with dice or darts is to score an even number
to take revenge and square things up

explanation.definitionFit: One reading is literally to obtain an even number; the idiom means to take one's revenge.

clue.text: Pressure for Eastenders to acquire Aussie English

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End pronounce the vowel of this word differently

parts.note: pressure is strain

explanation.surface: Stress for the cast of a TV soap trying to learn an Australian accent.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a London soap, but here Eastenders are Cockneys, whose 'strain' sounds like STRINE, the word Australians use for their own accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Strine is the jocular name for broad Australian speech, from how Aussies say Australian.

clue.text: Mother Earth's temperament

explanation.definitionFit: Nature is both the natural world, Mother Nature, and a person's basic disposition.

clue.text: Key ingredient of cheese is the sweetener

indicators.note: the key is placed inside the cheese as an ingredient

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A recipe says the vital ingredient of a cheese is the sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: A bribe is an inducement, colloquially a sweetener offered to win favour.

clue.text: Rent possibly frozen, firstly, for long-distance migrant

indicators.note: the frozen word is to be placed first

parts.note: the frozen polar region is the Arctic

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Rent is likely to be frozen first, says a migrant tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' scrambles the rent, and 'firstly' says the frozen word goes in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back each year, the longest migration of any bird.

clue.text: Some chance this, regularly, to find tuna, for example

indicators.note: every other letter is taken, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Some chance of finding tuna fish regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuna here is not fish but the prickly-pear cactus of Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is the name of a prickly pear, a kind of cactus; cacti are plants of that family.

clue.text: Set 1 across in a northern stream

definitions.meaning: to set alight is to set on fire
in Scotland and northern England a stream is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: To burn is to set on fire; a burn is also a Scottish word for a brook.

clue.text: Monster therefore is overthrown

indicators.note: overthrown in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: A monster is overthrown, so the story ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore.

clue.text: Free meal, without a starter — Scotland's own

indicators.note: the first letter of the meal is dropped

parts.note: lunch is a meal
ain is the Scots word for own

explanation.surface: A free Scottish lunch, but no starter is included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without a starter' drops L from LUNCH to leave UNCH; AIN is Scots for own, as in 'my ain folk'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain is to release, i.e. set free from fetters.

clue.text: FA Cup match featuring the Lions?

definitions.text: FA Cup match featuring the Lions?

parts.words: FA Cup match featuring the Lions?
parts.note: an important football match is a ..., and lions hunted on safari are also ...

explanation.definitionFit: A major fixture is called a big game, and large animals hunted for sport are big game too.

clue.text: Small circle of heroic Young Conservatives take on the French

parts.note: an epic is a heroic tale, and epic means heroic
YC abbreviates Young Conservatives
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Heroic young Tories take on France.
explanation.definitionFit: In old astronomy an epicycle is a small circle whose centre moves round a larger one.

clue.text: This good doctor's associate sounds obscure

definitions.text: This good doctor's associate sounds obscure

parts.words: This good doctor's associate sounds obscure
parts.note: the doctor's evil other self, Mr Hyde, has a name that sounds like hide, to obscure

explanation.definitionFit: Dr Jekyll is the good doctor of Stevenson's tale whose alter ego Mr Hyde sounds like the verb hide.
